explanation: Compared with Chvátal's page (users.encs.concordia.ca/~chvatal/conjecture.html: no independence system contains an intersecting subfamily larger than its largest star) and Chang–Liu–Liu (arXiv:2609.19123: every hereditary family of subsets of a finite set has a largest intersecting subfamily that is a star). Decreasing is 'hereditary/down-closed', Intersecting is pairwise nonempty intersection (so ∅ is never in an intersecting family, as usual), and the conclusion 'some x with every intersecting G ⊆ F having |G| ≤ |{A ∈ F : x ∈ A}|' is equivalent to a star being a maximum intersecting subfamily (the star at x is itself intersecting). Nonempty α is needed and harmless. Faithful.
